Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:112007
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 4795 of 2023
Applicant :- Virendra Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.0326 of 2021, under sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 506, 120-B I.P.C., Police Station Manduadih, District Varanasi, during the pendency of investigation.
opennyai_summary.22_May_2023__arguments:
It is further submitted that in the Virendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103674476/
1 present F.I.R. it has been alleged that present applicant and his brother with other colonizer Ashok Verma executed sale deed of the aforesaid land in favour of other persons though in the subsequent F.I.R. she admits that she was in possession and even her mutation was also done in her favour but interference was made by co-accused Om Prakash @ Channu Singh as named in Crime No.13 of 2022.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It shows that the allegation made in the present F.I.R. against the present applicant is false and not supported with material.
Since investigation is going on and the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, both the F.I.R.s present and subsequent, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Virendra Singh, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report, if any, under section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
